Where nycourts.gov and nysenate.gov refused automated requests, official captures of those same pages in the Internet Archive were used, as the controlling hierarchy permits for official archived pages when current official material is unavailable.
whatThisDocumentIs: The decision record that settles the source identity of the document Edition 1.2 retains as MRTA-DESTRUCTION-REQUEST. The projection carried the identity key rcap-ny-mrta-destruction-request-c6947b129d as unresolved_identity, with issuingAuthority not_recorded_in_integrated_source_contract, revision REV-UNKNOWN, no bytes, no mime and authorityStatus repository_measurement_unavailable, and a prior pass on 2026-08-07 recorded that no current Office of Court Administration publication of it could be located. roleAndProcess.legalRole: APPLICATION — a participant-initiated written request that expunged marihuana conviction records be destroyed

statutoryHook.operativeTextVerbatim: Upon the written request of the individual whose case has been expunged or their designated agent, such records shall be destroyed.
statutoryHook.context: The sentence sits inside § 160.50(5)(b), 'Duties of certain state officials and law enforcement agencies', whose clause (i) first requires the chief administrator of the courts to notify DCJS and the appropriate police departments, district attorneys' offices and other law enforcement agencies of the vacatur, dismissal and expungement, and requires the records to be marked expunged. The destruction duty attaches to those record holders on written request.
statutoryHook.citationNote: The form and the landing-page heading cite § 160.50(5)(a), the expungement provision that makes a record eligible. The destruction right itself is in (5)(b)(i). Both are correct in their place and neither should be replaced by the other.

roleAndProcess.participantFacingDetail: The upper portion is applicant-completed. Below a rule reading '***FOR COURT USE ONLY – DO NOT WRITE BELOW THIS LINE***' sits a six-item clerk processing checklist that belongs to the court and must never be prefilled or exposed to a participant as an input.
roleAndProcess.signatoryDetail: The execution block is captioned 'DEFENDANT'S AFFIRMATION' and reads 'I affirm this ___ day of ______, 20___, under the penalties of perjury under the laws of New York … that the foregoing is true', above a single rule captioned 'Defendant Signature'. There is no attorney signature line and no agent signature line on the current form.

designatedAgentAnalysis.statuteBasis: § 160.50(5)(b)(i) grants the right to 'the individual whose case has been expunged or their designated agent'.
designatedAgentAnalysis.landingPageOnAgents: The instructions page says 'Either you or your attorney may submit the application' and, separately, 'If your attorney submits your application for you, your application must be notarized.'
designatedAgentAnalysis.resolution: Submission and signature are different acts and the issuer separates them. An attorney may SUBMIT. The current form provides no line for anyone but the defendant to SIGN. The earlier 2020 edition did carry a dual rule reading 'Signature of Defendant or Defense Attorney'; that dual line was removed in a later edition.
designatedAgentAnalysis.consequence: A packet must not present an agent-signature path on this form. Whether a court accepts an agent-signed application is an operational question the form does not answer.

officialDestination.destination: the New York court in which the person was convicted
officialDestination.verbatimFromTheForm: Submit your application to the Court where you were convicted. (NOTE: There is no application fee.)
officialDestination.verbatimFromTheLandingPage: Submit your application to the same court where you were convicted. Your application cannot be processed if you send it to a different court.
officialDestination.perCourtRule: The landing page adds: 'If you have eligible marihuana/cannabis convictions in more than one court, you must submit a separate application to each court to request destruction of your expunged marihuana/cannabis conviction records.' One application per court of conviction, not one per person.
officialDestination.centralOcaIntakeFinding: There is no statewide Office of Court Administration address, mailbox or portal for this application. OCA publishes the form; the court of conviction receives it.
officialDestination.downstreamRouting: The court reviews the application, returns an Acknowledgement of Application to Destroy Expunged Marihuana Conviction Record, and forwards the application to the prosecutor, the law enforcement agencies involved and, where the person was fingerprinted, DCJS. DCJS then writes to confirm destruction. This is corroborated by court-use checklist item 6 on the form itself, which reads 'Copies of application sent to prosecutor, law enforcement agencies and DCJS as applicable for further processing.'

submissionMethods: Electronically through the court's Electronic Document Delivery System (EDDS)
roleAndProcess.submissionEvidence: Enumerated on the landing page as the three ways to submit.
roleAndProcess.feeBasis: 'There is NO APPLICATION FEE' on the landing page and '(NOTE: There is no application fee.)' on the form face.
roleAndProcess.proofOfIdentityCondition: Because the case is already expunged, the court cannot process the application without proof the applicant was the defendant: a valid government-issued photo ID if submitted in person, or — per the landing page — notarization if submitted by attorney, through EDDS or by mail.

legalDesignConflictRaised.whatTheIntegratedMemoRecords: The ny_mrta_marijuana track records destination kind 'agency', name 'Office of Court Administration', with the detail 'A participant who wants destruction uses the Office of Court Administration's application to destroy a marijuana conviction record, which Edition 1.2 retains at MRTA-DESTRUCTION-REQUEST, and sends it to the Office of Court Administration. Nothing is filed in a court on either stage.' The geography venue field repeats 'The Office of Court Administration receives the destruction request.'
legalDesignConflictRaised.whatTheOfficialSourceEstablishes: The application is submitted to the court of conviction, one per court, by EDDS, mail or in person. OCA is the publisher of the form, not its recipient.
whatIsCorrectInTheMemoAndMustBeKept: That the vacatur, dismissal and expungement happen by operation of law under § 160.50(5)(a) — correct.
That the chief administrator of the courts notifies the record-holding agencies — correct, and it is § 160.50(5)(b)(i)'s first clause.
That destruction is not automatic and occurs on the written request of the individual or their designated agent under § 160.50(5)(b)(i) — correct, and correctly cited.
That the destruction request is the conditional second unit of a composed mechanism — correct and untouched.
whatIsWrong: The submission destination. It is the convicting court, not the Office of Court Administration.
The statement 'Nothing is filed in a court on either stage.' It is right about the automatic-expungement stage and wrong about the destruction stage.
The absence of the per-court rule, which is a participant-facing consequence: a person with convictions in two courts must send two applications.
legalDesignConflictRaised.composedStructureUnaffectedWhy: Nothing here changes that there is one composed CPL § 160.50(5) mechanism, that unit 1 is automatic-expungement process guidance, that unit 2 is a conditional participant-signed destruction request, or that the request is official_pdf_fill. Only the destination attribute and the sentence that follows from it are wrong.
legalDesignConflictRaised.correctedByThisJobWhy: NY.memo.json is expressly excluded by this job's stop condition and is not among its owned paths. The conflict is recorded and handed off.
legalDesignConflictRaised.handoffTo: the New York legal-design owner, as a dedicated memo-correction child job for Session A to create
exactCorrectionRequired: Change the ny_mrta_marijuana destination from kind 'agency' / name 'Office of Court Administration' to the court in which the person was convicted, retaining OCA as the publisher of the form.
Replace 'Nothing is filed in a court on either stage' with a statement that scopes the no-filing point to the automatic-expungement stage only.
Add the per-court rule: a separate application to each court of conviction.
Record the three authorized submission methods and the no-fee fact.
Record that the current form carries a defendant-only signature line even though the statute permits a designated agent, and that an attorney may submit but the form provides no agent signature line.
legalDesignConflictRaised.doNotApplyHere: This job neither writes nor drafts the memo text. The corrections above are the exact scope a memo child must cover, not a patch.

statutoryRouteCheck.question: Was CPL § 160.50(5) amended after MRTA in a way that changes or retires the destruction route?
statutoryRouteCheck.answer: No. The most recent revision of CPL § 160.50 is 2021-04-02, the MRTA amendment. The Clean Slate Act, L.2023 c.631, signed 2023-11-16 and effective 2024-11-16, added CPL § 160.57 and did not amend § 160.50(5). The destruction route is intact and is not retired.
statutoryRouteCheck.correctionToTheResearchPremise: The chapter number is c.631, not c.744.
